subject: Civil Engineering
title: Fire Resistance of Concrete
description: A short lesson to help you apply Fire Resistance of Concrete.

hook.text: Steel buildings collapse in fire. Concrete buildings survive — most of the time.

buildup.text: Concrete doesn't burn. It insulates the steel rebar inside from extreme heat.

discovery.text: At 600°C, concrete loses about 50% of its strength. At 1,000°C, it crumbles.

twist.text: High-strength concrete spalls explosively in fire — steam pressure blows off the surface.

climax.text: Polypropylene fibers melt in fire, creating escape channels for steam — preventing spalling.

punchline.text: Concrete resists fire better than any other building material — but it has limits.

quiz.question: Why does high-strength concrete spall explosively in fire?
options: The aggregate expands faster than the cement paste
Dense concrete traps steam pressure that builds up and blasts off the surface
High-strength concrete contains flammable chemical admixtures
